# Work planning API

All paths are prefixed with `/api/v1`. Sessions send `X-Crew-Request: 1` for mutations. Work uses the shared people permission service and domain event bus. See [issue, label and discussion endpoints](api-work-issues.md).

## Projects and workflows

`GET /projects` lists accessible projects, optionally `orgId`, `archived=true` or `archived=all`. `GET /orgs/:orgId/projects` lists one organization. Filtering happens before opaque cursor pagination (`limit` up to 200, `cursor`). Guests see only explicitly granted projects.

`POST /orgs/:orgId/projects` creates `{key,name,description?,statuses?}`. Keys are normalized uppercase, 2–12 letters/digits beginning with a letter, unique within an organization. The default ordered workflow is Todo (todo), Doing (active), Done (done). Owner/admin permission `project:manage` is required.

`GET /projects/:projectId` returns `{project,permissions}`. Projects expose stable id, orgId, key, name, description, archived, nextIssueNumber, createdAt, updatedAt and ordered statuses. Each status exposes id, projectId, name, category and position. `PATCH` accepts key/name/description/archived/statuses. A key is immutable once an issue has been numbered. Archive hides a project from the default list; restore with `{archived:false}`. `DELETE` removes the project and guest grants and emits its final event.

`GET /projects/:projectId/workflow` returns statuses. `PUT` accepts `{statuses:[{id?,name,category}]}` in desired order. Preserve existing IDs to rename/reorder statuses. New entries omit ID. Names must be unique, and at least one todo and one done category must remain. A status containing an issue cannot be removed; move those issues first. Workflow replacement is atomic.

Read requires `project:read`; project configuration requires owner/admin `project:manage`. Role access and token scopes both apply. Every mutation emits actorId/orgId/projectId/entityType/entityId/action/before/after/time.

## Boards and atomic bulk edits

`GET /projects/:projectId/board` returns the project and ordered columns `{status,issues}`. Query `q` and `assigneeId` filter cards. `POST /issues/:issueId/move` accepts `{statusId,beforeId?}` or `{statusId,afterId?}`. No anchor appends. Anchors must belong to the destination column. Ranks use fractional insertion, deterministic ID tie-breaking, and an atomic rebalance when precision is exhausted. Every move emits a full issue before/after event.

`POST /projects/:projectId/issues/bulk` accepts `{issueIds,changes:{statusId?,assigneeId?,labelIds?},addLabelIds?,removeLabelIds?}`. Null assignee clears assignment; labelIds replaces labels, add/remove edits preserve others. Replacement cannot be mixed with add/remove. Every referenced issue/status/assignee/label is validated before a single transaction applies all changes. Cross-project issues and invalid edits leave every selected issue unchanged. Each modified issue emits its complete event. Both actions require `issue:write` and reject archived projects.

The board at `#/projects/:projectId/board` supports native drag/drop, pointer drag, per-card keyboard move menus, search/assignee filters, and selected-card bulk status/assignee/label forms. Errors remain visible and refresh follows successful persistence.

## CLI

`crew project list [--org ID] [--archived true|all] [--limit N] [--cursor CURSOR]`, `create --org ID --key KEY --name NAME [--description TEXT] [--workflow FILE]`, `show ID`, `update ID [--key KEY] [--name NAME] [--description TEXT] [--archived true|false]`, `archive ID`, `restore ID`, `delete ID --yes`, `workflow ID`, and `workflow-set ID --file FILE` use the same API and permissions. Workflow files contain a JSON status array. `crew board show PROJECT [--q TEXT] [--assignee ID]`, `board move ISSUE --status ID [--before ISSUE|--after ISSUE]`, and `board bulk PROJECT --issues ID,ID [--status ID] [--assignee ID|none] [--labels ID,ID|none] [--add-labels ID,ID] [--remove-labels ID,ID]` expose the board actions. All commands support global `--json`, `--url`, `--token` and `--config`.
